pcs.pc_description: Diagnose faults based on customer interaction, usage pattern (e.g. heavy-duty blending, food processing, juicing) and initial inspection, including smart display errors if present
Unplug the appliance and reset the overload switch or electronic safety lock to original state if triggered
Perform basic tests including voltage level check, ampere draw test, grounding test, and check smart diagnostics if available
Detect common electrical faults such as improper/no earthing, damaged power cord, defective switch panel or PCB, internal wiring issues, loose connectors, and blown fuses
Identify reasons for unusual sound or vibration during operation such as damaged coupler, unbalanced blade, worn-out bearings, loose jar lock, or motor alignment issues
Diagnose non-start conditions due to motor burnout, faulty speed control module, tripped safety switch, smart sensor errors, or power issues
Check for causes of jar content overflow or leakage such as improper lid fitting, damaged silicone gasket, sensor failure in auto-lock lid, or overloading in high-speed modes
Examine indicator panel or touchscreen for fault messages, LED codes, or app-based diagnostics if present
Test each module (motor unit, jar sensors, control board) individually when faults are not found through general checks
Escalate or send the appliance to factory service if faults involve embedded electronics or require advanced diagnostics not feasible on-site
Replace/repair faulty components like electronic control board, relay, temperature sensor, or timer at location using correct ESD precautions
Reschedule service if spare parts (e.g. smart PCB, non-standard jars, digital speed knob) are unavailable at site
Reassemble and verify that all components (e.g. jars with interlocks, smart lids, touchscreen panel) are functioning as per specifications
Demonstrate smooth operation of the appliance across all functions (grinding, juicing, food processing, smart modes) and validate through customer usage test
Explain safe handling of high-speed modes, jar locking mechanism, cleaning procedures for blade and sensors, and proper care of digital panels
Fill in digital or physical customer acknowledgment including QR-code warranty or AMC registration if applicable
Complete complaint/service documentation, including logging in service app or company CRM
Collect payment digitally or in cash as per organizational policy and issue invoice
Promote and inform the customer about new models, compatible accessories (multi-jar sets, spare lids), and AMC plans through app or catalog

pcs.pc_description: Diagnose faults based on customer interaction and usage pattern, including features such as inverter-based cooking, convection/grill usage, auto- cook programs, or app-based controls.
Unplug the appliance and ensure safe disconnection before initiating inspection and fault diagnosis.
Perform essential electrical tests like voltage, current, and earthing checks, and test for consistent power output in inverter-based systems.
Detect electrical or power faults such as improper/no earth, damaged power cord, surge damage, faulty power PCB, or loose/open contacts, especially in smart or digital units.
Diagnose no-heating issues due to inverter circuit failure, HV diode/capacitor breakdown, magnetron failure, faulty transformer, or blown fuses in traditional or inverter types.
Identify low-heating problems caused by ageing magnetron, cracked magnets, damaged dome, or inverter board issues.
Identify intermittent heating or sensor-based failures due to oxidized connections, burned terminals, or faulty inverter output control.
Detect touch panel or display malfunctions, faulty control boards, sensor errors (e.g. temperature/humidity), and software glitches in programmable or smart microwaves.
Inspect individual modules (e.g., inverter board, control PCB, sensor board, power supply) when fault is not evident through initial checks.
Forward the unit to an authorized service center for advanced component testing, firmware issues, or factory-only repairs.
Replace/repair components like inverter PCBs, control boards, relays, sensors, or heating elements at site if diagnosed and parts are available.
Schedule follow-up service if specific smart control boards, inverter units, or grill/convection parts are not immediately available.
Reassemble unit and verify full functionality of all systems, including heating modes, smart sensors, fan motors, touch controls, and app connectivity if applicable.
Demonstrate all features post-repair: microwave, grill, convection modes, digital touch interface, auto-cook programs, and mobile app control (if supported).
Instruct customer on cleaning procedures for sensors, grill elements, and fan filters; guide on regular maintenance and safe usage of inverter/convection features.
Obtain digital or written customer acknowledgment and satisfaction confirmation.
Complete service documentation including digital logs, firmware updates (if done), and repair summary.
Collect payment and issue invoice via app or POS system, if applicable.
Recommend AMCs or upsell accessories like grill stands, microwave-safe containers, or upgraded models if the unit is outdated.
